item.title: Mahmoud Khalil lawsuit says Columbia University failed to protect pro-Palestinian activists
item.description:
Lawsuit accuses university of ‘deliberate indifference’ and failure to respond to ‘persistent and coordinated harassment’ Mahmoud Khalil announced on Monday that he’s sued Columbia University , accusing the New York City school he attended of a years-long history of anti-Palestinian discrimination, indifference to harassment, and retaliation. Khalil, a US green card holder of Palestinian descent, was a graduate student at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) when he was arrested at his university apartment by federal immigration agents in March 2025, the first of a number of foreign nationals that the Trump administration has detained and sought to deport over their pro-Palestinian advocacy. item.title: Russian strike on passenger train will not deter Ukraine’s backers, Nato chief says
item.description:
Mark Rutte says attack that narrowly missed Boris Johnson and David Petraeus shows Vladimir Putin’s desperation The head of Nato has said a Russian drone attack on a train close to Ukraine’s border with Poland would not deter Kyiv’s western backers. Mark Rutte said the strike on a passenger train showed how desperate Vladimir Putin had become. “He thinks that he can stops us from supporting Ukraine and that he can undermine our unity. He is wrong. Our answer is to increase support,” the Nato general secretary said. Continue reading...

item.title: Dangote refinery launches Africa’s biggest IPO for retail investors
item.description:
The News Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote tapped the opening gong this morning on the floor of the Lagos exchange to open Africa’s largest initial public offer. The $20 billion Dangote Refinery built on swamp land on the outskirts of Lagos becomes the fourth Dangote Industries subsidiary to go public in Nigeria. When the initial offer closes next month, the company will have raised more than $4 billion at about a $50 billion valuation, if demand matches the year-long buzz partly driven by the company’s pledge to pay dividends in US dollars. The refinery will likely account for up to 40% of the Lagos exchange’s capitalization when its shares start trading post IPO in November. “We are going to fully, fully share all our prosperity with the people,” Dangote, 69, said in a packed and celebratory hall of bankers, investors and stock brokers for whom the multibillion-dollar Dangote…

item.title: Why talks in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states were postponed
item.description:
Impasse comes amid growing Saudi anger with Tehran over Houthi advances and strikes on airbase and pipeline Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut down Saudi Arabia’s east-west pipeline Gulf states have postponed a critical meeting with Iran on the future of the strait of Hormuz owing to a lack of Arab consensus and growing Saudi Arabian anger with Tehran for helping the Houthis loosen Riyadh’s grip in Yemen. The stalemate over the vital waterway came as Houthi rebels launched a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets. A Houthi military spokesperson claimed its forces had attacked the King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait, hitting fighter-jet hangars, radar systems, runways and landing strips, ammunition depots and additional targets. item.title: Rep. Jasmine Crockett’s praise of Chris Brown hit a nerve
item.description:
What happened: Rep. Jasmine Crockett, a Texas Democrat, took the stage in Arlington, Texas, on Saturday to honor R&B singer Chris Brown, delivering official congressional remarks highlighting his career. (She also honored Usher, but people are generally not mad about that.) “Right now, we are experiencing Black joy to the highest level,” Crockett said, according to video of the event. “And I wanted to make sure we document that in the Congressional Record.” Why are people mad: Brown pleaded guilty to felony assault of then-girlfriend Rihanna in 2009. Rihanna was hospitalized after injuries she sustained in the altercation, and a judge issued a restraining order. It’s probably the most well-known incidence of violence in his career but far from the only one. Brown was involved in a January 2013 altercation with singer Frank Ocean. item.description:

item.title: Texas governor threatens to penalize datacenters not obeying water laws
item.description:
Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use Greg Abbott , the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use. “Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he added. item.title: Rights group accuses Israel of dismantling 'Palestinian existence' in West Bank
item.description:
Israeli rights group B'Tselem said Monday that Israeli actions in the occupied West Bank form part of a greater project designed to make it impossible for Palestinians to exist together as a people. In a report titled "The Elimination Project", the group alleged five connected Israeli tactics and policies in the West Bank: "violence, ethnic cleansing, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction". FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

Sources: France 24, NPR
